text: Fixed. `Interval.fromISO` (src/interval.js) called `DateTime.fromISO` unguarded, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` a duration-only ISO interval ("2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M") threw instead of falling back to the Duration parse. It now parses each side defensively and falls back to Duration.fromISO, so valid intervals work and genuinely unparsable input still throws InvalidIntervalError. (Also fixed the "asISO 8601" typo in the invalid explanation.)

Fixed. In `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS` reverted the 19XX legacy year by doing `setUTCFullYear(getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which kept the day resolved against the leap year 2000; for a date like 0100-03-01 that produced Feb 29 of a non-leap year, so `plus({ days: 61 })` from 0099-12-31 landed a day early. It now re-sets the full year/month/day (`setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`). Verified by differential testing of `plus`/`minus` across the year-100 barrier.

Fixed. `DateTime#isInDST` (src/datetime.js) compared the current offset against the offsets of the same day-of-month in January and May, so for a year where DST covers that day (e.g. the US in 1974, DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27) the comparison was always against the same offset and it returned false. It now compares against the 1st of January and the 1st of May, i.e. against the year's standard-time offset, so 1974 reads as in-DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27 while ordinary years (and southern-hemisphere zones) still report correctly.

Fixed. The conversion matrices in `src/duration.js` were missing entries, so some unit pairs produced NaN: `casualMatrix.quarters` had no `seconds` (91*24*60*60) and both `casualMatrix.years` and `accurateMatrix.years` had no `quarters: 4`. `Duration#normalize` (and `shiftTo`/`as`) now works for every unit pair; verified by iterating all 9x9 pairs in both conversion accuracies.

Fixed. `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` padded the string form of a negative number, so `-100` (already 4 chars) was left as "-100" and `-5` became "00-5". It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign, so `DateTime#toISODate()` gives "-0100-05-25" / "-0005-05-25" while 5+ digit years ("-118040-05-25", "+118040-05-25") are unchanged.

Fixed. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` (src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js) was hard-coded to `true`, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset was accepted and `DateTime#setZone` produced a bogus DateTime. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`, so `new FixedOffsetZone("blah").isValid` is false and a DateTime set into such a zone is invalid ("unsupported zone").
